master.content:
ARMENIA DAILY MEDIA REVIEW

 

Subject: Main headlines in Armenia on 17-21 February 2023

 

FOREIGN RELATIONS

1) EU launches civil mission to Armenia - On 20 February, the European Union launched the EU civilian mission in Armenia (EU Mission in Armenia/EUMA) under the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), the Council of the European Union said in a press release.  The EUMA was formally established by a Council Decision on 23 January 2023. Through its deployment on the Armenian side of the Armenia-Azerbaijan border, the objectives are to contribute to stability in the border areas of Armenia, build confidence and human security in conflict affected areas, and ensure an environment conducive to the normalisation efforts between Armenia and Azerbaijan supported by the EU.  The total exclusively civilian - staff of the EUMA will be approximately 100, including around 50 unarmed observers.  The Operational Headquarters of the mission will be in Yeghegnadzor, in Armenia s Vayots Dzor province. EEAS Managing Director of the Civilian Planning and Conduct Capability (CPCC) Stefano Tomat will serve as the Civilian Operation Commander, while Markus Ritter will serve as the Head of Mission. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

2) EU monitoring mission in Armenia to contribute to stability and peace - Secretary of Security Council.(Armenpress 21/02)

 

3) Vice Speaker Rubinyan briefs MEPs on humanitarian challenges in blockaded Nagorno Karabakh.(Armenpress 21/02)

 

4) Ararat Mirzoyan and Stefano Tomat discuss issues related to the new EU civilian monitoring mission - On February 20, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Armenia Ararat Mirzoyan received the delegation headed by Stefano Tomat, the Civilian Operations Commander of the European External Action Service of the EU.  Markus Ritter, Head of Mission of the European Union Mission in Armenia, was also present. Issues related to the EU's new civilian monitoring mission were at the core of the discussions held during the meeting. "Highly appreciating the decision to deploy a long-term EU civilian mission in Armenia, Minister Mirzoyan expressed confidence that the mission will make an important contribution to stability in the region and ensuring the safety of the population living in the border regions with Azerbaijan," the message reads. Reference was also made to the overall security situation in the region and the efforts of Armenia and the international community aimed at establishing peace. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

5) Armenian Deputy FM, EEAS Civilian Operations Commander highlight EU mission for establishing border stability. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

6) Josep Borrell referred to the launch of the EU mission in Armenia - We launched the EU Mission in Armenia #EUMA, which is now operational and conducted its first patrol today. #EUMA will contribute to human security, build confidence on the ground and support EU efforts in the peace process between Armenia and Azerbaijan, he wrote on his Twitter page. (NEWS.AM 20/02)

 

7) Maria Zakharova comments on the deployment of EU civilian observation mission in the border regions of Armenia.(Armenpress 20/02)

 

8) Pashinyan meets with Prime Minister of Iraq and President of Iraqi Kurdistan - PM Pashinyan met with the PM of the Republic of Iraq Mohammed Shia al-Sudani in the side-lines of the Munich Security Conference. The parties emphasized the need to deepen trade and economic ties. An agreement was reached to organize a meeting of the Armenian-Iraqi intergovernmental commission in the near future. Pashinyan also met with President of Iraqi Kurdistan, Nechirvan Barzani. The interlocutors highlighted the importance of constant development of trade and economic cooperation. An exchange of views on other topics of regional significance took place. (Arminfo 17/02)

 

9) PACE co-rapporteurs visit Armenian settlements affected by Azeri aggression. (NEWS.AM 20/02)

 

10) Armenian Minister of Defence, U.S. Defence Security Cooperation Agency Director discuss possibilities for cooperation - Armenian Minister of Defence Suren Papikyan met with the United States Department of Defence s Defence Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA) Director James Hursch during the IDEX and NAVDEX 2023 defence exhibition in the United Arab Emirates. A number of issues related to the possibilities of military-technical cooperation were discussed at the meeting, the defence ministry said in a press release. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

11) New delegation from European Parliament to visit Armenia on fact-finding mission. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

12) Governor of Shirak holds meeting with Russian Ambassador - Governor of Shirak Mushegh Muradyan held a meeting with the Ambassador of Russia in Armenia Sergei Kopyrkin. The Governor talked about the friendly relations between the two countries and the programs implemented in Shirak, Muradyan s office said in a read-out. Issues related to the prospects of trade-economic, educational and cultural relations were discussed. An agreement was reached to organize new meetings to implement new joint initiatives. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

13) Armenian Deputy FM presents the vision of Armenia on the future of the Eastern Partnership at the 10th regular session of the "Euronest" Parliamentary Assembly. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

14) The new United States Ambassador to Armenia Kristina Kvien presented the copy of credentials to the Foreign Minister of Armenia Ararat Mirzoyan on February 20. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

15) PM Pashinyan, Senator Menendez discuss the humanitarian crisis in Artsakh [Nagorno-Karabakh] - Within the framework of the Munich Security Conference, PM Nikol Pashinyan had a meeting with Bob Menendez, chairman of the US Senate Foreign Relations Committee. The interlocutors discussed the developments taking place in the South Caucasus region, the situation around NK. (Armradio 19/02)

 

16) Continued blockade of Lachin corridor could lead to irreversible humanitarian consequences, Armenian PM says in Munich - It s already 70 days that the Lachin corridor has been blocked, and now, unfortunately, we have a humanitarian and energy crisis in Nagorno Karabakh , Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said at a panel discussion on Moving Mountains? Building Security in the South Caucasus held on the sidelines of the Munich Security Conference. The electricity and gas supplies to Nagorno Karabakh have been shut down, and during the last 70 days the gas supply has been cut at least ten times, and it is a problem that should be addressed. Our position is that in the trilateral statement from November 9, 2020, we have very precise provisions connected with the Lachin corridor, and according to that statement, it is the obligation of Azerbaijan and Russian peacekeepers to keep the Lachin corridor operable. But now, unfortunately, we have totally different situation, PM Pashinyan said. The situation should be in the focus of international attention, because we are afraid that the continuation of the situation can cause irreversible humanitarian consequences for Armenians in Nagorno Karabakh, the Prime Minister said. (Armradio 18/02)

 

17) Pashinyan, Aliyev, Blinken hold trilateral meeting in Munich - Prime Minister of Armenia Nikol Pashinyan, US Secretary of State Antony Blinken and President of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev held a trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Munich Security Conference. At the meeting, reference was made to the progress of work on the draft peace treaty between Armenia and Azerbaijan, as well as the unblocking of regional transport infrastructure and the implementation of delimitation between the two countries in line with the agreement reached in Prague.  PM Pashinyan reaffirmed the determination of the Armenian side to achieve a treaty that will truly guarantee long-term peace and stability in the region.  At the same time, Pashinyan emphasized the fact of Azerbaijan s illegal blockade of the Lachin Corridor and the resulting humanitarian, environmental and energy crisis in Nagorno-Karabakh.  Ensuring the continuity of the peace process between Armenia and Azerbaijan was emphasized. (Armradio 18/02)

 

18) Armenian, Latvian leaders meet in Munich. (Panorama 18/02)

 

19) Armenian FM briefs USAID official on humanitarian crisis in Nagorno-Karabakh.(Panorama 18/02)

 

20) EU to send 100-strong civilian mission to Armenia - The European Union plans to send a 100-strong civilian mission to Armenia next week, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said after a meeting with Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan. "Next week, the EU will send a 100-strong mission contributing to peace and stability," she said in a tweet. President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen said that the EU is a committed partner of Armenia and it will develop further the potential in the Economic Investment Plan. (Armenpress.am 18/02)

 

21) Pashinyan briefs OSCE chief on humanitarian crisis in Nagorno-Karabakh - Armenian PM Nikol Pashinyan and OSCE Secretary General Helga Schmid held a meeting in Munich. The parties touched on the activities of the civilian mission of the European Union in Armenia and expressed hope that it will contribute to the strengthening of peace and stability, the Armenian government said in its readout of the meeting. The sides exchanged views on the processes taking place in the region and other issues of mutual interest, the statement added. (Panorama 18/02)

 

22) Armenia deputy PM, OSCE Chairperson-in-Office Personal Representative discuss regional matters. (NEWS.AM 17/02)

 

23) EU to support negotiations on peace treaty: Michel and Aliyev discuss EU mission in Armenia - The European Union will continue its efforts to normalize relations between Armenia and Azerbaijan, European Council President Charles Michel said during his meeting with Azerbaijani President Aliyev on February 17.  The European Union will also continue its efforts towards holding talks on a peace treaty and ensuring stability and security in the South Caucasus.  The sides also exchanged views on the activities of the European Union mission in Armenia. (NEWS.AM 17/02)

 

24) Pashinyan holds brief meeting with Macron in Munich - On the sidelines of the Munich Security Conference, Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan on Friday had a short meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron. The interlocutors exchanged ideas on regional security and stability issues, the premier's office reported. (Panorama 17/02)

 

25) Russia ready to host a meeting of Armenian, Azerbaijani FMs At a weekly briefing, Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova highlighted that both Armenian and Azerbaijani officials reaffirmed their interest in Russia's mediation in the talks on a peace treaty between the two countries at meetings with Russian Foreign Ministry special envoy Igor Khovayev in Yerevan and Baku. Zakharova stressed that Russia is ready "to organize another meeting in Moscow between the foreign ministers of Armenia and Azerbaijan on this matter." (Panorama 17/02)

 

26) His Holiness Aram I visits quake-affected Aleppo. (Armradio 17/02)

 

27) CoE Deputy Secretary General briefed on ongoing blockade of Artsakh [NK] - Vice President of the Armenian National Assembly, Head of the Armenian Delegation to the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) Ruben Rubinyan, held a meeting with Council of Europe s Deputy Secretary General Bjørn Berge. The interlocutors exchanged views on regional issues and the normalization of Armenia-Turkey relations. The sides reaffirmed their commitment to continuing the effective collaboration in a number of directions. (Armradio 17/02)

 

28) Armenian Speaker Lauds Council of Europe - Speaker of Armenia s National Assembly Alen Simonian hosted Kimmo Kiljunen (Finland, SOC) and Boriana Åberg (Sweden, EPP/CD), co-rapporteurs of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE), at the start of their fact-finding visit to Armenia. Simonian praised the co-rapporteurs for urging an immediate end to the blockade just days after Azerbaijani government-backed protesters halted traffic through the corridor on December 12. He also noted with satisfaction that a PACE committee will release on soon a report on humanitarian consequences of the blockade. (Azatutyun.am 17/02)

 

29) ICRC head tells PM Pashinyan organization will continue to contribute to solving problems in Nagorno-Karabakh. (NEWS.AM 17/02)

 

30) Europol head expresses satisfaction with cooperation with Armenia at meeting with Pashinyan. (News.am 17/02)

 

 

INTERNAL DEVELOPMENTS

31) Armenia's History Museum to host temporaryexhibition on Karabakh movement. (Panorama 18/02)

 

32) Retired army general detained on charges of money laundering - Grigory Khachaturov is under arrest amid an ongoing criminal investigation. The investigation concerns his tenure as commander of a military base from 2006 to 2010. Major-general Khachaturov was the Commander of the 3rd Army Corps from 2016 to 2021. (Armenpress 21/02)

 

33) Two Armenian soldiers killed in military car crash - Two Armenian servicemen were killed and two others were injured in a military car crash near the village of Khnatsakh in Syunik Province late on 19/02, the Defense Ministry reported.  The UAZ vehicle carrying the soldiers rolled into a ravine because of an avalanche at around 7:40pm, the ministry said.  (Panorama 20/02)

 

34) Armenian SAR operations in quake-hit Turkey and Syria: 3 survivors, 20 bodies retrieved from rubble - Lieutenant colonel Garik Aghramanyan, Chief of the Operational Shift at the National Center of Crisis Management delivered a briefing on the Armenian search and rescue (SAR) operations carried out in quake-hit Turkey and Syria. The SAR teams included doctors, K9 specialists, experts of radiation, chemical and biological situation monitoring. The teams were equipped with food, water, tents, equipment and other devices for 7-day self-sustainable operations.  (Armenpress 20/02)

 

35) Chief of New Armenian Police Force sacked. (Azatutyun.am 17/02)

 

36) Opposition leader unimpressed By Turkish-Armenian Dialogue - A senior member of the main opposition Hayastan alliance downplayed the significance of the latest Turkish-Armenian negotiations, saying that Ankara is sticking to its preconditions for normalizing relations with Yerevan. Gegham Manukian, a lawmaker representing Hayastan insisted that Ankara only made symbolic gestures to Yerevan. The Armenian authorities are trying to present those gestures to their citizens as historic developments, he said. But as the joint news conference of Cavusoglu and Mirzoyan showed, Turkey is continuing to condition its relations with Armenia by negotiations between Azerbaijan and Armenia and to speak in the same language of preconditions. (Azatutyun.am 17/02)

 

37) Armenian President makes staff changes in RA MoD. (Arminfo 17/02)

 

 

NAGORNO KARABAKH

38) ICRC facilitates transfer of patients from blockaded Artsakh.(Armenpress 21/02)

 

39) Russian peacekeepers deliver over 35 tons of humanitarian aid to Nagorno Karabakh - The Russian Aerospace Forces transported the humanitarian cargo collected by the We are United multinational project - from Russia to the Armenian capital of Yerevan. Then, the Russian peacekeepers transported the 35 tons of food products to Stepanakert through the Lachin corridor. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

40) Karabakh Leader rejects Aliyev s condition for talks - Nagorno-Karabakh s leadership has rejected Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev s condition for direct negotiations between Baku and the authorities in Stepanakert.  Speaking during the Munich Security Conference at the weekend, Aliyev said he will agree to such talks only if Ruben Vardanyan, the Karabakh premier, resigns and leaves our territory. Vardanyan is a criminal oligarch who was smuggled to Karabakh from Russia, he told a panel discussion with the prime ministers of Armenia and Georgia.  Prime Minister Nikol Pashinian did not react to Aliyev s condition during the discussion.  A spokeswoman for Arayik Harutiunian, the Karabakh president, said Vardanyan s current role is Artsakh s internal affair and can in no way be a topic of discussion for the government of Azerbaijan.   Lusine Avanesian told the Artsakhpress news agency that Aliyev himself is suspected for good reason of corruption and war crimes. Avanesian said his comments about Vardanyan are an attempt to legitimize Azerbaijan s blockade of the sole road connecting Karabakh to Armenia. (Azatutyun.am 20/02)

 

41) President Harutyunyan, State Minister Vardanyan and Speaker Tovmasyan visit Stepanakert memorial.(Armenpress 20/02)

 

42) We must do everything to make the cherished dreams and goals of our heroes come true President of Artsakh (Nagorno Karabakh) Arayik Harutyunyan released a statement on the occasion of the 35th anniversary of the Karabakh Movement. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

43) Ruben Vardanyan: Our will to keep Artsakh [NK] Armenian remains unshakable - Artsakh s State Minister Ruben Vardanyan issued a message on Artsakh [NK] Revival Day and the 35th anniversary of the Karabakh movement marked on February 20, stressing if not for the Karabakh movement, we would have lost not only Artsakh [NK], but also Armenia. (Panorama 20/02)

 

44) Karabakh movement saved hundreds of thousands of lives: President Sargsyan s message on movement s 30th anniversary - President of Armenia Serzh Sargsyan addressed a message on the Artsakh [NK] Revival Day and the 30th anniversary of the Karabakh movement. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

45) Robert Kocharyan issues Artsakh Revival Day message - Armenia s second President Robert Kocharyan issued a congratulatory message on Artsakh [NK] Revival Day and the 35th anniversary of the Karabakh movement marked on February 20. (Panorama 20/02)

 

46) Artsakh [NK] Foreign Minister conducted visit to Russia last week - From 12 to 16 February, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Artsakh [NK] Sergey Ghazaryan was on a working visit to the Russian Federation, the Foreign Ministry of Artsakh [NK] said in a press release. During the visit, the Foreign Minister had meetings with public, political, and expert circles, as well as representatives of the Armenian community. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

47) Artsakh s [NK] FM visits Yerablur Pantheon - On the occasion of the 35th anniversary of the Karabakh Movement, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Artsakh [NK] Sergey Ghazaryan, who remains in the Republic of Armenia due to the ongoing blockade, visited Yerablur military pantheon and on behalf of the people and authorities of Artsakh [NK] placed a wreath in memory of those who gave their lives for the independence and freedom of the Motherland throughout the National-Liberation Struggle of Artsakh [NK]. (Armenpress 20/02)

 

 

ECONOMIC HEADLINES

48) European Investment Bank ready to discuss implementation of new projects in Armenia - PM Nikol Pashinyan had a meeting with the President of the European Investment Bank Werner Hoyer in Munich. Werner Hoyer assessed the cooperation with the Armenian government as effective and noted that the EIB is ready to discuss the possibilities of implementing new projects in different directions with Armenian partners. (Armradio 18/02)

 

49) EBRD forecasts 4% GDP growth for Armenia in 2023. (PanARMENIAN.Net 17/02)

 

50) ITB Berlin warns Armenia against distributing "material of a political nature" at ITB Berlin 2023 - Vice-Chairman of the Republican Party of Armenia (RPA) Armen Ashotyan posted a letter by ITB Berlin 2023 to Armenia's Ministry of Economy. (Arminfo 18/02)

 

51) IDEX 2023: Eighteen Armenian companies showcase defense solutions at UAE exhibition.(Armradio 20/02)

 

52) Armenia Posts Double-Digit Growth.(Azatutyun.am 20/02)

 

53) FlyOne Armenia: Largest national carrier by destinations, passenger count plans major expansion, including India flights- In 2023, FlyOne Armenia will launch roundtrip Yerevan-Dusseldorf flights, will restore the full schedule flights to Beirut, and will also fly to Tehran, Novosibirsk and Samara, according to Flyone Armenia Chairman of the Board Aram Ananyan. (Armenpress 21/02)

 

 

This review includes information published by the Armenian media and does not represent the views of the Delegation.
